title: Rider Account Rule: Open On-Demand Trips and Reservations Held at Once (Wayfare Rides)
content:
**Rule.** On **Wayfare Rides (rider trips and fares)** a rider may hold any number of trips over time; every trip is its own record and is charged on its own. There is no limit on the number of trips a rider may take over time.

1. A new on-demand request is accepted only when the rider has no other on-demand trip in requested, accepted, driver arrived or in progress status.
2. A reservation is accepted only while the rider holds fewer reserved trips in scheduled or accepted status than the most open reservations allowed on the ride option being reserved; reservations and one open on-demand trip may coexist.
3. Trips of different riders are never combined, and one trip never carries charges for another trip.

The most open on-demand trips and the most open reservations are figures of each ride option.

## Basis of the checks

- Both checks are decided from the system's trip records for the rider (the rider, each trip's status and whether it was booked on demand or reserved), as they stand before the new request or reservation; the rider's own account of what is open does not replace those records.
- Each new trip is a separate record with its own request time; an earlier trip of the rider is never reused for a new request.
- The reservation check compares against the figure of the ride option **being reserved**, not the option of the rider's other reserved trips.

## Judgement table

| What the rider's records show | New on-demand request | New reservation |
|---|---|---|
| An on-demand trip in requested, accepted, driver arrived or in progress status | Not accepted | Decided by the reservation count alone |
| No on-demand trip in any of those statuses | Accepted, as far as this rule goes | Decided by the reservation count alone |
| Reserved trips in scheduled or accepted status fewer than the reserved option's figure | — | Accepted, as far as this rule goes |
| Reserved trips in scheduled or accepted status equal to the reserved option's figure | — | Not accepted |

## Worked cases (hypothetical)

- A rider has one completed trip and one reserved trip in scheduled status, and asks for an on-demand ride. Neither is an open on-demand trip, so this rule does not stop the request.
- A rider holds five reserved trips in scheduled or accepted status and tries to reserve a ride option whose figure is 5. Five is not fewer than 5, so the reservation is not accepted. Had the option's figure been 10, it would be accepted under this rule.
